news.title: 🔴 ALERT — CISA Warns: Hackers Are Actively Exploiting On-Prem SharePoint — Patch Now
news.excerpt: CISA added a critical on-prem SharePoint flaw (CVE-2026-56164) to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalog after active attacks. If your org runs SharePoint on its own servers, patch now and rotate machine keys — or pull outside access until you can.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — New 'CrashStealer' malware hijacks your Mac by faking Apple
news.excerpt: A new macOS infostealer called CrashStealer spreads through fake "Werkbit Setup" sites, impersonating Apple's CrashReporter to steal passwords, browser data, and crypto wallets. If you see "CrashReporter.dmg" in Downloads, don't open it.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday Fixes 570 Flaws, 3 Zero-Days
news.excerpt: Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday is the largest in company history: 570 flaws fixed, including 3 zero-days — 2 already exploited in the wild. If you run Windows, Office, Exchange, or SharePoint, install updates TODAY.

news.title: Six Zero-Days Live: Patch These Now
news.excerpt: Six vulnerabilities are already under active attack today (July 13, 2026) — including flaws in Adobe ColdFusion, Langflow, and a cluster of Joomla extensions. If you run any of those tools, isolate them. Everyone else: stop hitting "remind me later" on updates.

posts.headline: Lost laptop? BitLocker can be bypassed in minutes — install the July Windows Update to close the hole
posts.tip: Turn on BitLocker drive encryption (search “BitLocker” in the Start menu, or Settings > Privacy & Security > Device encryption) and install the July 2026 Windows Update at Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates. The patch for CVE-2026-50661 blocks a physical-attack bypass that let someone with brief hands-on access read or change an encrypted drive.
posts.truth: Most people figure BitLocker turns a stolen laptop into a paperweight. It helps — but on an unpatched machine a thief with five minutes and a screwdriver can get around it. Encryption is not a substitute for a strong password and the latest patch. The update that closed this hole shipped July 14, and I still see machines that haven’t pulled it.

posts.headline: Chrome’s July 2026 update closes 382 security holes — update at chrome://settings/help
posts.tip: Open Google Chrome and update it right now: type chrome://settings/help in the address bar (or Menu > Settings > About Chrome) and let it download the latest build. Chrome’s July 2026 releases (150/151) patched close to 400 bugs, including critical code-execution flaws that let a malicious page run code on your PC.
posts.truth: Folks patch their phone the day an update drops but leave Chrome three versions behind for a year. Your browser touches every site you visit — it’s the most exposed program on your computer, and the one most people never update. An old Chrome is an open window.

posts.headline: Florida storm season: an APC Back-UPS keeps your computer alive when the power goes out
posts.tip: Put your computer on an APC Back-UPS battery unit — grab a BE550G or BX series from apc.com or Amazon, or have Onyx install one. It rides through a blackout and soaks the voltage spikes that roll in right after the lights flicker.
posts.truth: I see more dead motherboards and fried power supplies after a storm than from anything else all year. A $60 battery backup beats a $600 board repair every single time, and it’s the one upgrade most North Florida folks skip until the surge does the choosing for them.

posts.headline: Turn any PDF or webpage into a study podcast free — Google NotebookLM at notebooklm.google.com
posts.tip: Go to notebooklm.google.com with your Google account, drop in a PDF, Google Doc, or web link, and ask it to summarize or build an Audio Overview. It’s free, and every answer points back to your source material.
posts.truth: Everybody’s scared AI will just make stuff up. NotebookLM won’t — it only reads what you give it and shows you the citation. For students, researchers, or anyone buried in a 60-page manual, it’s the rare AI tool that actually earns its keep instead of guessing.

posts.headline: Stubborn app won’t go away? Revo Uninstaller Free deletes it and the traces
posts.tip: Download Revo Uninstaller Free from revouninstaller.com/products/revo-uninstaller-free and use it to remove programs Windows can’t fully uninstall — it scrubs the leftover files and registry entries the built-in uninstaller leaves behind.
posts.truth: Windows’ own uninstaller leaves a graveyard of leftovers — folders, registry keys, startup junk — that slowly gunks up a machine. “It’s uninstalled” rarely means “it’s gone.” Revo actually cleans the corpse instead of just hiding it.

posts.headline: Stop feeding ad-trackers your data — uBlock Origin blocks ads and trackers free inside Firefox
posts.tip: Install uBlock Origin for free from `addons.mozilla.org` — open Firefox, press `Ctrl+Shift+A` to reach Add-ons, search "uBlock Origin," and click Add. Out of the box it blocks ads, cross-site trackers, and coin-miner scripts with almost no memory cost.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize the "free" web is paid for by watching everything you do. An ad-blocker isn't about killing ads — it's about stopping strangers from building a file on you.

posts.headline: Find out if your email is already in a data breach — Have I Been Pwned checks it free in 10 seconds
posts.tip: Go to Have I Been Pwned at `haveibeenpwned.com`, type your email address, and hit "pwned?" — it checks your address against billions of breached accounts and tells you exactly which breaches exposed it. No signup, no cost.
posts.truth: The honest answer is your password was probably leaked years ago in some breach you forgot about. Checking isn't scary — not checking is what gets you hacked.

posts.headline: Run private AI on your own PC — LM Studio is the free desktop app that keeps your chats off the cloud
posts.tip: Download LM Studio free from `lmstudio.ai`, install it, pick a model like Llama or Qwen from its built-in catalog, and start chatting — everything runs on your machine. No account, nothing leaves your PC.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize every "free" AI website is reading what you type. If it's private, run it locally. LM Studio makes that stupid-easy — no command line, no PhD required.
